options_evaluated: Monomaterial unreinforced polymer (e.g., pure ABS or PP)
Co-molded multi-material polymer (e.g., ABS with TPE overmolding)
assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial unreinforced polymer (e.g., pure ABS or PP) with molded-in material identification codes
assessments.rationale: Using a single, unreinforced polymer maximizes the ease and quality of recycling (Annex I (d)) and avoids solutions detrimental to recycling (Annex I (e)). Co-molded elastomers and fiber reinforcements act as contaminants in mechanical recycling streams, downgrading the quality of the recovered plastic or making it completely unrecyclable. Unreinforced polymers also minimize microplastic and nanoplastic release (Annex I (p)) during EOL shredding compared to fiber-filled composites.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Design and Manufacturing (which prefer overmolded grips for ergonomics and tactile feel, and fiber-reinforced plastics for thin-walled structural strength and weight reduction).

options_evaluated: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws with metal inserts)
assessments.recommendation: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws with metal inserts)
assessments.rationale: Reversible mechanical fasteners facilitate non-destructive disassembly, which directly supports the ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing, and refurbishment (Annex I (c)). It also enhances the ease and quality of recycling (Annex I (d)) by allowing recyclers to quickly and cleanly separate different material fractions (e.g., copper motors, PCBs, plastic housings) at end-of-life, avoiding the mixing of incompatible materials.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (which prefers ultrasonic welding or snap-fits to minimize assembly cycle times, part count, and production costs).

options_evaluated: Standard brushless DC (BLDC) motor with glued magnets
Modular brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable magnet and copper assemblies
assessments.recommendation: Modular brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable magnet and copper assemblies
assessments.rationale: Brushless motors offer superior durability compared to brushed motors, which wear out quickly and generate carbon dust (microparticles) during operation and EOL treatment (Annex I (p)). To ensure high-quality recycling (Annex I (d)), the BLDC motor must be designed for disassembly so that high-value copper windings and critical raw materials (neodymium magnets) can be cleanly extracted rather than lost in shredder residue.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing and Cost (which prefer integrated, glued BLDC motors or cheap brushed motors to reduce component costs and simplify assembly).

options_evaluated: Active cooling with potted electronic control units
Passive cooling with large, unpotted aluminum heatsinks
Forced-air cooling using main suction airflow with open, conformal-coated PCBs
assessments.recommendation: Forced-air cooling using main suction airflow with open, conformal-coated PCBs
assessments.rationale: Potting compounds (resins/silicones) are highly detrimental to EOL treatment (Annex I (e)) because they permanently encase electronic components, making component-level repair, refurbishment (Annex I (c)), and pyrometallurgical recycling of precious metals impossible. An open PCB design cooled by the vacuum's airflow allows for easy disassembly, testing, repair, and high-quality recycling of both the board and the aluminum heatsinks.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Reliability and Use Phase (which prefer potted electronics to guarantee complete protection against fine dust and moisture ingress, potentially extending use-phase reliability in harsh environments).

options_evaluated: Semi-modular design with soldered wire harnesses
Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play functional modules
assessments.recommendation: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play functional modules
assessments.rationale: A fully modular architecture allows individual functional blocks (e.g., motor, cord reel, battery, switch assembly) to be independently serviced, repaired, or remanufactured (Annex I (c)), preventing the entire vacuum cleaner from becoming premature waste (Annex I (r)). At EOL, modularity reduces the energy and resources required for sorting and processing (Annex I (g)) by allowing rapid manual separation of high-value components.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Design and Manufacturing (which prefer integrated monolithic designs to achieve a more compact product footprint, sleeker aesthetics, and lower material/assembly costs).

assessments.rationale: Corded AC power completely avoids the use of lithium-ion batteries, which are the shortest-lived components in modern vacuums and carry a massive environmental footprint in EOL treatment (Annex I (m)). Eliminating the battery prevents significant hazardous waste generation (Annex I (r)) and avoids the energy-intensive hydrometallurgical recycling processes required for battery recovery. If cordless is mandatory, a user-removable, standardized battery pack is the only acceptable alternative to prevent premature product disposal.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Use Phase and Marketing (which heavily favor cordless battery-powered models for user convenience, portability, and market demand).
